historicalScope: Original unbranded design interpretations suitable for an around-2000 Japanese balcony/utility area. Dimensions and manufacture are modeling assumptions, not certified engineering data or exact historical SKU replicas.

assets.manufacture: Assumed outdoor corn/sorghum-fibre broom: turned hardwood handle enters a compressed fibre shoulder, retained by natural-fibre collar and three physical binding wraps. Individual tapered fibres form the fan rather than a texture card.
assets.components: hardwood handle and pommel, compressed binding collar, three wraps, individual tapered broom fibres
assets.mounting: Free standing diagnostic pose with fibre tips normalized to y=0; later scene placement may lean against the apartment wall but must preserve floor contact.
assets.interfaces: Handle penetrates the compressed shoulder intentionally; fibre roots terminate inside the bound collar. No floating fibre roots. Bend/load mechanics are not simulated.
assets.orientationExposure: Handle and outer fan exposed to midsummer sun/sky; dense inner fibres and wall-facing side are sheltered after placement.
assets.agingCausality: Dry maintained state. Frayed tips, dust accumulation and handle polish require location/use history; no arbitrary dirt or damage is baked.
assets.geometryVsMaterial: Handle diameter, collar, bindings and every retained fibre are geometry. Fine wood/fibre grain and roughness are material.

assets.manufacture: Assumed injection-molded polypropylene dustpan represented as a sloped scoop floor, separate thick sidewalls/rear wall, rounded front lip, load ribs and an upright molded handle with a real hanging aperture.
assets.components: closed sloped scoop, rounded front lip, two sidewalls, rear wall, handle with through-hole, two load ribs
assets.mounting: Free standing on the scoop/front bearing geometry at y=0. Handle is upright and unrigged.
assets.interfaces: Walls and ribs intentionally enter floor/rear join volumes; the hanging aperture is actual topology, not a dark decal. Exhaustive injection-mold draft and interference simulation is pending.
assets.orientationExposure: Open scoop faces outward/upward during use and catches dust; underside and wall-facing rear surfaces are sheltered when stored.
assets.agingCausality: Intact dry reference. Edge polish and dust streaks require later use/contact evidence.
assets.geometryVsMaterial: Scoop slope, lip, wall thickness, ribs and hanging aperture are geometry; molding grain is material.

assets.manufacture: Assumed shaped hardwood hand scrub brush with a raised palm grip and individually bundled stiff bristles inserted into the underside. Bristle density reduces by LOD but the block/grip remain physical.
assets.components: rounded wood block, raised palm grip, individual tapered bristles grouped into deterministic tufts
assets.mounting: Free standing on bristle tips at y=0 for diagnostic viewing; usable pose can lie on wood side or bristles depending scene context.
assets.interfaces: Bristle roots penetrate the block underside intentionally to model drilled/stapled retention. Grip overlaps block as a shaped join. No loose/floating bristles.
assets.orientationExposure: Bristle tips/contact face exposed to water/dirt in use; upper wood grip exposed to hand wear and sun during drying.
assets.agingCausality: Dry maintained state. End wear, wet swelling, darkened bristle tips and soap residue are deferred until causal scene state is defined.
assets.geometryVsMaterial: Block, grip and retained bristle strands are geometry; wood grain and bristle microsurface are material.

lodPolicy: MASTER plus LOD0/1/2/3 are actual separate exports. LOD reduction primarily reduces fibre/tuft counts and radial/path segmentation while retaining manufactured component identity.

externalVerification.preview: actual GLB diagnostic raster with backface culling; not Unity or Visual Fidelity evidence
